description: Akashi Code Reality Check: tells an AI coding agent whether the packages, versions and symbols it is about to use actually exist, across npm, PyPI, crates.io, Go, Maven, RubyGems, Packagist and NuGet. POST /v1/check with {"language","code"} (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust) returns a diagnostic per import and call: nonexistent package, likely typo-squat, placeholder, suspiciously new, deprecated or nonexistent symbol. POST /v1/package(s), /v1/versions and /v1/symbol(s) answer single questions (exists, latest, yanked, deprecated, the real alternatives). Every response is a JSON object, errors included ({"error":{"code","message","retryable"}} with 4xx). Upstream outages give partial results listed in unavailable, never a 5xx.

rpc_types.backend_hint: akashi-api (FastAPI) on :8000, router at /code; relayer rest url http://<api-host>:8000/code
rpc_types.notes: Only GET /v1/version, GET /v1/health, POST /v1/check, /v1/package, /v1/packages, /v1/versions, /v1/symbol, /v1/symbols. Inputs only in the JSON body. Every response is a JSON object.

serving.backend: The akashi-api container (one image serves all three Akashi services under /cite, /code, /now) behind an HA RelayMiner whose rest backend points at /code. No auth toward the backend; callers cannot send headers. Needs outbound HTTPS to the eight package registries and a ts-introspect sidecar for TypeScript symbols.

healthcheck.notes: Functional probe: a hallucinated method on a pinned version.

serving.notes: p95 under 6.5 s, hard stop 7 s; request bodies up to 64 KiB. Gateway operators: configure as type passthrough with rpc_types ["rest"]; see deploy/gateway/sage-service.yaml.
